fieldMarks: Light brown back with small dark brown spots or streaks.
Light line from just behind the eye to the angle of the jaw; weak whitish dots along the side between the legs.
Tail flattened at the base and strongly keeled; belly whitish with light brown to gray speckling and a gradual back-to-belly colour transition.
behavior: Strongly aquatic; adults hide under rocks or logs in water or in splash-zone crevices, larvae and juveniles use smaller seeps.
Eats mostly worms, insects and crustaceans.
Females lay up to about 60 eggs (average 26) March-November and guard them; larvae metamorphose in about 2 years.
habitat: Small to medium mountain streams with rocky substrate, spring runs and roadside puddles in wooded mountain terrain at 300-1220 m; may forage in surrounding forest on wet evenings.
range: Eastern Kentucky, adjacent southwestern Virginia, southern West Virginia and eastern Tennessee (Cumberland Plateau and Mountains). Not in Canada.

lookalikes.name: Seal salamander
lookalikes.howToTell: Lighter belly giving a distinct back-to-belly contrast.

lookalikes.name: Northern dusky salamander
lookalikes.howToTell: Formerly treated as the same species; welteri has darker toe tips and a strongly keeled tail.
